verdict.rationale: Moss's first-party MCP server lets a user's AI assistant create indexes, add documents and run queries from inside a conversation. Its Vercel AI SDK integration also exposes Moss operations as tools a language model can call. So natural-language operation is possible, but it depends on an external assistant or LLM; Moss has no built-in natural-language interface of its own. missing for 10: native natural-language command interface in the product itself, documentation of which operations are covered by natural language, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Your AI assistant can create indexes, add documents, and run sub-10ms semantic queries without leaving the conversation.
This setup exposes Moss operations as AI SDK tools, so language models can search, create indexes, and manage documents as part of agentic workflows.
